reading.body:
UC Berkeley / vLLM Team's listed product is vLLM, categorized under open source & self-hosted models, with high-throughput inference engine as the function this data names first.

The data also tags vLLM with open-source and no external data sharing, description of what the product does rather than how well it does it. It also notes self-hosted, one of the few entries in this set where the product touches compute or physical infrastructure directly rather than sitting purely at the application layer.

Beyond the category, the product name, and this short list of tags tied to github.com, the data carries no user counts, revenue, funding, or headcount, so nothing here supports a claim about UC Berkeley / vLLM Team's scale or trajectory.

profile_text.body:
UC Berkeley / vLLM Team is listed as a university lab rather than a for-profit company, with its website given as github.com. The text harvested from that site describes GitHub as an AI-powered developer platform where developers, businesses, and an open source community build software, and says GitHub provides AI and automation tools to help build and ship software faster. That text describes GitHub itself, not the vLLM project or the team.

The one product tracked for the team is vLLM, described as a high-throughput inference engine that is open source and self-hosted, with no external data sharing. Its listed URL is the vllm-project/vllm repository on GitHub.

The profile data records no lawsuits and no MCP servers for the team.
